Dover.metaTitle: Wildlife Removal in Dover, NH | Strafford County Pros
Dover.metaDescription: Bats, raccoons, squirrels, rats and skunks in Dover, NH — Cochecho River mill city. Same-day service from our local crew.
Dover.housing_era: New Hampshire's oldest permanent settlement, a small mill city with 19th-century brick and mill-worker housing downtown, historic homes, post-war neighborhoods, and newer subdivisions.
Dover.geographic_features: Cochecho River (runs through downtown), Bellamy River (river in the west), Piscataqua River (tidal boundary to the east), Willand Pond (pond shared with Somersworth)
neighborhoods: Downtown (mill-era and historic homes)
Garrison Hill area (residential streets by the park)
West Dover (neighborhoods toward the Bellamy River)
Back River Road area (rural homes in the north)
Dover.wildlife_intro:
Dover's mill-city housing gives bats, raccoons and gray squirrels steady attic access, and its downtown brick blocks support mice and Norway rats around food businesses. Skunks and woodchucks work yards in the post-war neighborhoods, the Cochecho and Bellamy corridors move raccoons through town, and newer subdivisions see squirrels, moles and the occasional fisher. Opossums turn up under decks here in the southern tier.

Our crew plans Dover's many bat jobs around the state rule — no exclusion from occupied structures from May 15 to August 15 — inspecting in summer and excluding in fall. Winter drives rodents into the older housing hard, and spring brings chimney raccoons. Dover work often involves connected older structures, so inspections cover additions and shared rooflines, not just the room where noises were heard.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Dover, NH?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing or cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts.  Simple single-entry squirrel jobs cost less than full attic exclusion or bat work, and we never quote a firm figure before seeing the structure.

faqs.q: Are the rats in downtown Dover likely to get into nearby houses?
faqs.a: They can. Rats follow food, water and shelter, and older homes near commercial blocks offer all three through foundation gaps and utility openings. Our crew seals those openings, advises on food sources like bird seed and pet food, and handles removal — exclusion is what keeps a downtown rat problem from becoming a house problem.

Summer bat colonies in older homes are inspected, then excluded after the May 15 to August 15 restriction lifts. Our crew covers a lot of ground here, from downtown multifamily sealing to farmstead work on the rural roads.

faqs.q: We keep smelling skunk around our Rochester porch in winter. Is one living there?

Somersworth.wildlife_intro:
Somersworth packs a lot of older housing into a small city, and raccoons, gray squirrels, bats and mice are constant in its mill-era homes and multifamily buildings. Norway rats appear around older commercial and food areas, skunks den under porches across the neighborhoods, and the Salmon Falls River corridor moves raccoons and beavers through the low ground along the Maine line.

Because so many Somersworth buildings are multifamily, our crew inspects whole structures rather than single units — animals travel shared walls and rooflines freely. Fall sealing before the long winter is the highest-value work here, and bat jobs follow the state timing rule, with exclusion scheduled outside May 15 to August 15. Spring chimney raccoons and attic squirrel litters round out the busy season in this compact city.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Somersworth, NH?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing or cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts. Shared-wall buildings can cost more to seal fully, and we explain that scope up front. faqs.q: Our Somersworth duplex has bats in the attic. Does the whole building need work?
faqs.a: Usually yes. A shared attic means the colony uses the whole space, and entries can be on either side of the building. Our crew inspects both units' rooflines, plans one-way exclusion for after the restricted window, and seals every entry — doing half a duplex rarely keeps bats out.

Rural roads add woodchucks and the occasional fisher.

The academic calendar shapes our Durham work: fall move-in brings a wave of calls from rentals that sat empty or lightly watched all summer, and spring openings reveal overwinter mouse and squirrel damage. Our crew works with owners and managers on sealing and trash practices, because in a rental town the durable fix is a tight building and secured food, not one removal.

faqs.q: Why do Durham rentals get so many raccoon and skunk problems?

With lots this wooded, most jobs include checking outbuildings as well as the house — animals denied the attic often test the barn next.

The Cochecho River corridor moves raccoons and beavers through town, and foothill homes toward the Blue Hills see fishers and steady squirrel pressure from the surrounding woods.

Spring in Farmington brings woodchucks out and raccoons into chimneys, and summer bat colonies in the older homes are inspected for fall exclusion after the August 15 date passes. Fall is our crew's sealing season before the long, cold winter sets in. Farmington jobs often span the house and the barn — older farmsteads here offer animals several buildings to choose from, and securing only one rarely ends the calls.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Farmington, NH?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing or cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts. faqs.q: What animals cause the most trouble in Farmington barns?
